purpose: filegroup(data = ...) (rules/filegroup/Filegroup.java:48-119, FilegroupRule.java:36-80): `data` prerequisites are target-configuration edges that never add files to build; the default runfiles are Runfiles.Builder.addRunfiles(DEFAULT_RUNFILES) (Runfiles.java:663-781: each `data` prerequisite's files to build (--incompatible_always_include_files_in_data) and data runfiles, then each `srcs` prerequisite's default runfiles), the data runfiles the files to build then addRunfiles(DATA_RUNFILES) (--incompatible_filegroup_runfiles_for_data, CoreOptions.java:66-75); the executable stays the single file to build; Bazel 9.3's filegroup has no `path` attribute. Motivation: `build --nobuild //src/beyondwork.ai/...` on ~/code stopped at `@@rules_rust++rust+rust_linux_x86_64__x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu__stable_tools//:rust-lld: filegroup accepted at load time but not analyzed by the native profile: attribute 'data' = [...]` (the rust_toolchain's exec `linker`, whose gcc-ld/* linkers are data runfiles read as `linker[DefaultInfo].default_runfiles.files`, rules_rust rust/private/toolchain.bzl:273-294).

comparison (tests/filegroup_data.rs, liv: MATCH: success equal; WARNING lines equal in order; a failing case's genuine message (or the recorded part of it) (the `Error in <callable>: ` / `Error: ` Starlark text, else the rule error following an empty `in KIND rule L: ` line, else the first ERROR message) is contained in native stderr; built top-level outputs (path below bazel-out -> [mode, contents]) equal; a `test` case's stdout (the test summary, ` in N.Ns` run times as ` in <T>s`) equal; a successful `run` case's stdout (the program's output) equal; a `query` case's stdout equal; the recorded outputs' existence after the command equal. genuine_key_findings: fg(srcs a.txt, data d.txt): files [a.txt], default_runfiles [d.txt], data_runfiles [a.txt, d.txt], files_to_run.executable a.txt; several srcs: no executable, data in its order ([z.txt, d.txt]); data only: files [], both runfiles [d.txt]; ctx.files of filegroups lists files to build only.

A rule with runfiles in data: its files to build and data runfiles ([tool, t.txt]); in srcs with data d.txt: default_runfiles [d.txt, t.txt, tool] (data first, then the srcs' default runfiles), data_runfiles [tool, d.txt, t.txt]; a filegroup in data contributes its files to build and data runfiles ([a.txt, d.txt]), in srcs its default runfiles ([d.txt]); select() in data resolves per configuration.

A generated data file is built: as an action input of a consumer of the default runfiles (contents `pkg/gen.txt: gen.txt`), and by `build` of the filegroup itself (bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/pkg/gen.txt exists; the hidden top-level output group holds the default runfiles), whose result lists only its files to build (`up-to-date (nothing to build)` for source files).

Through an exec attribute (rules_rust's linker): files [pkg/t.txt], default_runfiles [bazel-out/k8-opt-exec/bin/pkg/gen.txt, pkg/d.txt]; a binary merging its data's default runfiles has [a.txt, d.txt, gen.txt, show, t.txt, tool] in its runfiles tree (`run`).

Visibility and testonly of a data prerequisite are the usual prerequisite errors; a missing data file is `missing input file '//pkg:missing.txt'` at execution (with --nobuild genuine succeeds); `query deps()` follows data; `path` is `no such attribute 'path' in 'filegroup' rule`.

Genuine: an aspect propagating along `srcs`/`data` visits [fg_nested, fg]; output_group selects the files to build ([groups.extra], executable groups.extra), data stays runfiles (default_runfiles [d.txt], data_runfiles [groups.extra, d.txt]) — native matches since filegroup `output_group` is modelled (tests/fixtures/filegroup_output_group).
known_divergences: Native prints its own result format (`LABEL\tPATH`, `bazel-rs: N actions executed ...`), no INFO lines; native result lines of source files are not compared (Bazel prints `up-to-date (nothing to build)`).
Declared divergences missing_nobuild and path: see the cases (pre-existing native limitations, not specific to `data`).
Native is passed --experimental-builtin-modules in every case (as in the other paired fixtures).
